16-year-old Josaia Croker excited to represent Fiji at Youth Olympic Games
item.description: 16-year-old Josaia Croker of Rotuma says it is an honour and privilege to represent Fiji at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar , Senegal as he balances his triathlon training with his schoolwork. The Marist Brothers High School student says his preparations for the Games are going well, despite the challenges of managing his academic commitments alongside his sporting ambitions.
item.content:encoded:
16-year-old Josaia Croker of Rotuma says it is an honour and privilege to represent Fiji at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar , Senegal as he balances his triathlon training with his schoolwork.

The Marist Brothers High School student says his preparations for the Games are going well, despite the challenges of managing his academic commitments alongside his sporting ambitions.

He says one of the biggest sacrifices he has had to make as a young athlete is spending less time with his friends so he can focus on training and studying .

Croker says his family has been very supportive of his journey and is helping him as he prepares to compete on the international stage.

He says he is excited about the opportunity to represent Fiji and is grateful for the chance to achieve this milestone at just 16 years old.

The 2026 Youth Olympic Games will be held in Dakar, Senegal, from 30th October to 13th November.

item.title: Fiji Bati thrash Cook Islands 40-12 in Rugby League World Cup opener
item.description: The Vodafone Fiji Bati have opened their Rugby League World Cup campaign with a convincing 40-12 victory over the Cook Islands at McDonald Jones Stadium in Newcastle. The Bati scored seven tries, with Waqa Blake, Jacob Saifiti, Taane Milne, Caleb Navale and Kitione Kautoga crossing the try line, while Solomone Saukuru scored a double.
item.content:encoded:
The Vodafone Fiji Bati have opened their Rugby League World Cup campaign with a convincing 40-12 victory over the Cook Islands at McDonald Jones Stadium in Newcastle.

The Bati scored seven tries, with Waqa Blake, Jacob Saifiti, Taane Milne, Caleb Navale and Kitione Kautoga crossing the try line, while Solomone Saukuru scored a double.

The Bati applied pressure on the Cook Islands from the beginning of the match, launching wave after wave of attacks and maintaining their intensity throughout the game.

Bati captain Apisai Koroisau says they knew they had to start fast and praised the players for their efforts on the field.

Koroisau says the team knew what they needed to do in the first half and executed their game plan well.

With Australia up next, Koroisau says the Kangaroos are at the top of the food chain for a reason, but the Bati will give everything they have on the field.

Wakeham was named Player of the Match after producing three try assists, two line breaks and four tackle breaks, alongside an impressive kicking performance.

The Bati will face the Kangaroos at Suncorp Stadium at 9.05pm next Sunday.

item.title: Fiji Bulikula fall 18-12 to three-time world champions Kiwi Ferns
item.description: The Vodafone Fiji Bulikula have gone down 18-12 to three time world champions New Zealand in their first ever Rugby League World Cup match. They were able to run in two converted tries to Losana Lutu and Sienna Laing in the first half.
item.content:encoded:
The Vodafone Fiji Bulikula have gone down 18-12 to three time world champions New Zealand in their first ever Rugby League World Cup match.

They were able to run in two converted tries to Losana Lutu and Sienna Laing in the first half.

The Kiwi Ferns scored through Leaianne Tufuga, a double from Stacey Waaka and the other points from Zahara Temara's boot with the conversions and penalties.

Skipper Sereana Naitokatoka says the girls worked hard for their people, Vanua, and their families.

Naitokatoka says she is really proud of her team adding that where there is unity God commands his blessings.

Insert: Naitokatoka on pushing hard Oct 18

The Bulikula did not go out there to play a fancy game but just stuck to the basics and almost rocked the Kiwi Ferns.

The Bulikula are only the second team to lead the Kiwi Ferns at halftime.

Right now they have a few injury worries in the squad which they will need to look at before their next game.

The Bulikula will face the PNG Orchids next Saturday at 3.15pm at Santos National Football Stadium, Port Moresby.

item.title: Kaile Auvray re-signs with Extra Bula FC for 2027 season
item.description: Kaile Auvray will return to Extra Bula FC for the 2027 OFC Professional League season after an impressive debut campaign with the Bula Warriors. The 22-year-old was one of the club's standout performers during its inaugural season , bringing pace, creativity and attacking flair to the side.
item.content:encoded:
Kaile Auvray will return to Extra Bula FC for the 2027 OFC Professional League season after an impressive debut campaign with the Bula Warriors.

The 22-year-old was one of the club's standout performers during its inaugural season , bringing pace, creativity and attacking flair to the side.

Auvray played an important role in helping Extra Bula FC finish third in the regular season and qualify for the Top Four playoffs.

He says he is excited to return and looks forward to working with his teammates to build on their performances from last season.

Auvray believes maintaining consistency within the squad will be important as the team aims to achieve better results in its second season.

Auvray says he is looking forward to sharing the field with his teammates again, adding that the opportunity to play together should not be taken for granted.

His return provides continuity for Extra Bula FC as the club prepares for its second OFC Professional League campaign which will begin in January.
